subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 20, September 10th, 2026, Certified by its maker. Audited that day.
body:

What degraded

  • The deck ships UNDER its own bar, at 6.76 against 6.8
    Five rounds is the cap in scoring_rubric.yaml and past it a round may repair a hard fail and nothing else. There were no hard fails in rounds 3, 4 or 5. The spread across the three final judges is 0.328 and the criterion holding it down is artwork_craft at a median of 6.5, weighted 0.28.
  • Four things three judges asked for and this run did not do
    Slide 1's razor-straight horizon seam and a declared focal the band below it is measurably lighter than. Slide 9's unworn pass, which carries half the close's argument and reads at 432px as a block rather than a tyre print. The two-part contact shadow on frames 3, 6 and 8, which the craft judge calls the technique's own named failure and which is one of this deck's three declared structural laws. And the door's address: slide 9 says any interested person may petition NHTSA and never prints 49 CFR 552.3, while slide 6 already prints 49 CFR PART 555 in its own footer.
  • The deck is set in ranch country and the story is in Austin
    Six frames are footered TRAVIS COUNTY or AUSTIN and the drawn world across all nine is caliche, cedar and a cattle guard, against the opening law of TEXAS_VERNACULAR.md. The no-vehicle rule did not require leaving the city and a curb, a block or limestone would have honoured both. Found by the round 5 reader judge.
  • An accumulated verdict that is WRONG, recorded so the next run does not act on it
    Three judges across two rounds called slide 5 cuttable. Round 5's craft judge read the same evidence and reached the opposite conclusion, and it is right: the duplication is real but it is a COPY defect, and slide 5's surface is the best drawn thing in the deck and the value arc's floor. Rewrite slide 5's dek. Do not cut slide 5.
  • The run stopped mid flight, and it was not a permission prompt
    Measured, 1,224 dispatches, none waited on a human, slowest permissionDecisionMs 44 ms. What happened is that the session ENDED ITS TURN to write progress reports, which from outside is the same event: the run waits for a person who is not there. prompt_audit measures permission waits and a turn that simply ends leaves nothing to measure, so it reports clean on exactly this.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Certified by its maker. Audited that day., paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Tesla certified its own Cybercab.

Tesla put a small number of Cybercabs into commercial service in Austin on September 3rd, 2026, and told NHTSA it had certified them as compliant with all applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. The Office of Defects Investigation opened Audit Query AQ26002 the same day. An audit query is not a defect investigation and it is not a recall.

Zoox self-certified a robotaxi with no steering wheel and no pedals in 2022. It later filed for a temporary Part 555 exemption from eight federal standards. Final approval came in July 2026. Zoox did both, in that order.

The audit examines the process and the technical data behind Tesla's certification. Under 49 CFR 552.3 any interested person may petition NHTSA to decide whether a vehicle meets an applicable standard. Which standards did Tesla read as inapplicable?

#AQ26002 #FMVSS #Part555

Notes

THE RECORD. 123 items. tx-2026-0140 and tx-2026-0141 admitted, tx-2026-0126 and tx-2026-0130 promoted, 16 items re-verified, 12 movement notes re-worded. Four claims were re-pointed off the commission's rolling calendar feed after the September 4th deadline came off it, which is what that feed does once a date passes. THE WORST THING FOUND, and it was on the record rather than the deck. tx-2026-0140's title published the audit as opening "on the day paid driverless rides began in Austin". No claim on the item carries the word paid and none describes how the vehicle drives. The carousel struck that same word from its own cover in scoring round 1 for exactly that reason, and the record went on keeping its own copy until a round 3 judge read the docket item. Fixing a word on a frame is half the fix. HOUSE STYLE WENT RED ON THE REBUILD. Eleven sentences across seven items ran 31 to 44 words against a 30 word backstop, all of them this run's own admissions and movement notes. Split at a clause and clean. THE PANEL TOOK FIVE ROUNDS and the useful number is not the median. Rounds 1 to 5 went 6.808, 6.570, 6.772 and 6.760, and the spread across three judges closed from 0.694 to 0.160 before widening to 0.328 at the end. Both of round 2's hard fails were made by round 1's own repairs. Rounds 3, 4 and 5 carried none at all. ROUND 4 WAS NET NEUTRAL ON CRAFT AND ITS OWN JUDGE SAID SO. Four of five changes were typographic. The hairline that round added to slide 2 is invisible at 432 pixels, checked on the thumb, and the slide 8 line move traded one proximity error for a worse one. That is the pattern the rubric's own header warns about. FIVE DECLARATIONS CONTRADICTED THE CODE THEY NAME and round 5 repaired all five, because a false statement in a committed file is not a craft note and the round cap does not protect it. aggregates.json carried slide 6's old dimension scale for a whole round after the repair that changed it. slide 9's probe published the marked band under the name of the unmarked one. The caption's own citation walked past a completeness claim that only reads frames. Slide 7's claim strip cited two claims that do not carry the line above it. The storyboard said 23 verified against 24 and restated a deck median rather than measuring it. FOUR ACCEPTANCE ITEMS ASSERTED MEASUREMENTS NO FRAME HAD DECLARED. data-encodes and data-contacts appeared in four of the plan's most checkable items and in none of the nine frames, so render_report's encodings and contacts were empty arrays and the four items were checking nothing. All four are declared now and measure dE 28.9, dL* 23.8, dE 16.4 and dE 31.0. A GATE NOBODY RUNS IS A GATE THAT IS RED. construction_check.py is in neither guards.yml nor the routine's phase list, so it went unrun until scoring round 3 and had been red the whole time at 5 of 9 frames against a threshold of half. The four decks before this one measure 2, 1, 4 and 1, so the finding was real rather than a drifted threshold. THE DOOR. The record's own public_access says a member of the public can read the resume and go to the same office, and the deck carried only the first half, so its close was a lookup dressed as an action. nhtsa.gov returns 403 to this run's fetcher on every page tried and the AQ26002 resume carries no complaint boilerplate, so the door is 49 CFR 552.3 from Cornell instead, which is narrower and better: the rule under which any interested person asks the agency to decide whether a vehicle fails to comply with an applicable standard. The reserved red stays unspent, because red is for a dated door. THE PROMPT AUDIT, taken last so it covers the whole run. Full reading in the email above.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
